title: Fatal shooting justified after police officer acted in self-defence: ASIRT
subtitle: Alberta's police watchdog says an RCMP officer acted in self-defence when he shot and killed a 30-year-old man during a traffic stop south of Edmonton in the summer of 2013.
article: Alberta's police watchdog says an RCMP officer acted in self-defence when he shot and killed a 30-year-old man during a traffic stop south of Edmonton in the summer of 2013.

A statement released Tuesday by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team said the string of events began when a truck sped by the lone RCMP officer as he was parked on the highway near Ma-Me-O Beach on Aug. 3, and one of the passengers gave him the finger out the window.

When the officer tried to pull over the vehicle, it continued down the driveway of a home before stopping. ASIRT says the driver was unable to produce a valid driver's licence, and appeared to be drunk.

ASIRT says the officer asked the man to get out of the vehicle. The man's three adult sons got out of the vehicle as well. When the officer told the man he was being arrested for impaired driving, the man "became more agitated," ASIRT says, and said "I don't wanna go." As the officer and the driver began to struggle, the man's sons "moved quickly toward the police officer." The officer drew his gun and pepper spray, and told the men "to get away or he would shoot them."
The driver of the truck then got into the police car where the officer's shotgun was located.
Fearing for "his own personal safety, the police officer fired three rounds from his RCMP service pistol, striking two of the advancing men," the report reads.
The officer was then able to get back in his car, where he called for backup and ambulances.
ASIRT says one of the men got back in the truck and pursued the officer a short distance down the highway.
ASIRT said the string of events lasted less than 2 1/2 minutes, and was captured on audio recording.
The ASIRT report also says no racial slurs were used by the officer during the events, that the driver was never handcuffed during the incident, and that the officer did not Taser any of the men.
Because of the remote rural location, it took several minutes for emergency crews to get to the area.
The 30-year-old died from two gunshot wounds. His 41-year-old brother was found injured a short distance away, and was taken to hospital by STARS Air Ambulance. He survived his injuries.
Both men had high levels of alcohol in their blood.
The ASIRT report says the original suspect truck tried to drive through one of the RCMP roadblocks about 1 1/2 hours after the shooting.
When the officer noticed the man appeared to be drunk and tried to arrest him the man, he said, "So what," began swearing, and began punching the officer.
The driver was then Tasered, handcuffed and taken into custody.
A statement by ASIRT executive director Susan Hughson concluded the RCMP police officer was acting properly and that the use of force was justified.
"This finding in no way diminishes the sad fact that a family has lost their loved one," the statement read.

Family members previously identified the man who died as Lance Cutarm, the injured man as his older brother Larron, and the driver as their father, Larry Cutarm. The other man in the car was identified at that time as the family's youngest son, Lee.

As a teenager, Lance Cutarm was convicted of manslaughter for the 1999 stabbing death of 18-year-old Michael Coutereille, who was stabbed by Cutarm when he went to check on a commotion in the hallway of his apartment building.

Larry and Larron Cutarm were convicted in 1994 of aggravated assault in the beating death of 32-year-old Charles Rowan. The men were from the nearby Pigeon Lake First Nation. A statement released by RCMP on Tuesday extended sympathy to the family of the deceased, and quoted assistant commissioner Marlin Degrand as saying the situation had been "extremely difficult for everyone, including the officer involved."
"Our hope is that ASIRT's independent investigation provides (the deceased's family) with a clearer understanding of this tragic event," he said.
